clinicalPearls: A hypomyelinating leukodystrophy caused by variants in TUBB4A, encoding a central-nervous-system beta-tubulin isotype, spanning a wide clinical spectrum

At one end is severe hypomyelination with atrophy of the basal ganglia and cerebellum (H-ABC); at the other are milder or isolated hypomyelination and the dominant dystonia syndrome DYT4 (whispering dysphonia with generalised dystonia and ataxia)
Milder cases may show hypomyelination on MRI with little or no striatal atrophy, so imaging appearances range from pure hypomyelination to the full H-ABC pattern of a shrinking putamen and caudate
Clinical features commonly include a movement disorder (dystonia, spasticity, chorea), cerebellar ataxia, dysarthria and variable developmental involvement
Most disease-causing variants arise de novo and are dominant, though inherited variants (including the DYT4 variant) occur, so family history may be positive or negative
Diagnosis is guided by recognition of a hypomyelinating pattern with or without basal ganglia and cerebellar atrophy, confirmed by TUBB4A sequencing
There is no specific therapy; management is supportive and multidisciplinary, targeting dystonia and spasticity, communication, nutrition and physiotherapy
reference.pathophysiology: TUBB4A-related disease is caused by dominant variants in TUBB4A, which encodes a beta-tubulin isotype highly expressed in the brain. Tubulin heterodimers assemble into microtubules that are essential for cell shape, intracellular transport and division. Variant tubulin perturbs microtubule dynamics in oligodendrocytes and neurons; disrupted oligodendrocyte function impairs myelin formation to produce hypomyelination, while neuronal microtubule dysfunction contributes to degeneration of the striatum and cerebellum in more severe cases. The particular variant strongly influences where on the spectrum a patient falls, from isolated hypomyelination to full H-ABC.
additionalDifferentials: Hypomyelination with atrophy of basal ganglia and cerebellum (the severe TUBB4A phenotype)
Other tubulinopathies and cortical malformation syndromes
Primary dystonia syndromes when the movement disorder dominates
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI to characterise the degree of hypomyelination and any basal ganglia or cerebellar atrophy
TUBB4A sequencing, including analysis for the recurrent H-ABC variant and the DYT4 variant
Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy gene panel or exome if TUBB4A is negative
Metabolic screen to exclude treatable causes of a hypomyelinating or movement-disorder phenotype
Movement-disorder assessment to guide symptomatic management
Speech, swallow and developmental evaluation as clinically indicated
redFlags: Status dystonicus with severe dystonia, pain and metabolic disturbance
Progressive dysphagia with aspiration and faltering growth
Rapid neurological regression suggesting intercurrent illness or an alternative cause
Respiratory compromise from bulbar and truncal involvement
reference.prognosis: Prognosis varies markedly across the TUBB4A spectrum: severe early-onset (H-ABC) disease is progressive with substantial motor and cognitive disability and reduced life expectancy, whereas milder hypomyelination and the DYT4 dystonia phenotype can follow a more indolent course. The specific variant is the main determinant of severity and rate of progression.
pitfalls: Not appreciating the breadth of the TUBB4A spectrum and expecting only the severe H-ABC picture
Overlooking basal ganglia atrophy or, conversely, excluding the diagnosis when striatal atrophy is absent in milder cases
Assuming autosomal recessive inheritance when most variants are de novo dominant
Missing the DYT4 dystonia phenotype as part of the same gene's spectrum
Failing to counsel families about recurrence risk, including germline mosaicism
references: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: Manage the movement disorder symptomatically, treating dystonia with agents such as trihexyphenidyl or baclofen and using botulinum toxin for focal dystonia
Provide physiotherapy and occupational therapy for spasticity, ataxia and mobility, with orthoses and aids as needed
Offer speech and language therapy for dysarthria and swallow assessment with nutritional support where feeding is impaired
Provide developmental support and manage any seizures
Coordinate multidisciplinary neurology-led follow-up across the wide clinical spectrum
Offer genetic counselling, noting most variants arise de novo while some, including the DYT4 variant, are inherited dominantly
